newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Malaysian suspected as parcel bomb hurts two in NZ.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian suspected as parcel bomb hurts two in NZ.

text.p: New Zealand police said on Thursday they were focusing on a Malaysian suspect in a parcel bomb explosion that injured two Malaysian students in Wellington.
"We have a suspect who we believe to be domiciled in Malaysia," Detective Inspector Brett Kane said.
The two students, a woman of 20 and a man aged 25, were taken to hospital with burns on Wednesday after the parcel bomb, collected from a courier company, exploded in their car.
Kane said the package was mailed from Kuala Lumpur, and he was pursuing inquiries through the international police network Interpol to find out where it came from within Malaysia.

He said the parcel was addressed to the female student and was designed to cause serious injury. The suspect was a man who had briefly met the victim and who had also visited New Zealand earlier this year.
Kane declined to speculate on the motive but said: "In a broad sense I can say that there is a domestic element to it."
He said forensic experts were examining the parcel bomb and he planned further contact with Interpol on Friday.
